subject: How can I combine two methylBase objects in methylKit

messages.author: 7d06ae1690d45e6a
messages.subject: How can I combine two methylBase objects in methylKit
parts:
Hi,
I’m trying to pool a subset of my low coverage samples to create new pooled samples that I can then use with my high coverage samples for differential methylation.

I have two groups - control group has samples A, B, C and test group has samples D, E, F
I’ve can pool the low coverage samples A and B as well as D and E in the groups using reorganize() and pool() into ctl.lo and test.lo in a meth.lo methylBase object.
I can similarly create a meth.hi methylBase object with samples C and F (the high coverage samples).

What is the best way for me to combine meth.lo and meth.hi into a meth.pool or similar so I can run differential methylation on these.
Thanks,
Piali

messages.author: 7d06ae1690d45e6a
messages.subject: Re: [methylkit_discussion] How can I combine two methylBase objects in methylKit
parts:
Figured this out:
myobj.pool=methRead(file.list, sample.id=list("A","B","C","D","E","F"),
               assembly="mm10",pipeline="amp",treatment=c(0,2,0,3,1,1))
meth.forpool=unite(myobj.pool,destrand=F)
pool.trickery <- pool(meth.forpool, sample.ids=c("A.B","C","D.E","F"))
pool.trickery <- reorganize(pool.trickery, sample.ids=c("A.B","C","D.E","F"), treatment=c(0,0,1,1))

Cheers,
Piali
